tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting up a fictional wastewater plant after an overnight shutdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: whole plant, from log review to normal operation.

cards.label: Remove lockout devices by authorized staff and restore power to units
Verify flows, tank levels, and effluent quality before settling into normal operation
Open the influent isolation gate gradually
Start preliminary and primary units as flow arrives
Inspect screens, pumps, and blowers for readiness
Start aeration blowers and return sludge pumps for the biological units
Review the shift log and check for outstanding alarms

tasks.explanation: Alarms and lockouts are cleared first, equipment is checked before flow is admitted, units start in flow order, and verification confirms the plant is stable.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a planned shutdown of one treatment unit for maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one unit being isolated while the rest of the plant keeps treating flow.

cards.label: Drain and flush the isolated unit
Divert influent flow to the remaining units or holding capacity
Stop chemical feeds serving only the unit being isolated
Test the atmosphere and confirm safe conditions if entry is required
Notify the supervisor and affected staff of the planned isolation
Open the unit for maintenance work
Apply lockout and tagout to the unit equipment

tasks.explanation: Flow is diverted before the unit is emptied, lockout follows draining, atmospheric testing comes after isolation, and only then is the unit opened for work.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for restarting the plant after a utility power outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: power has just been restored after a two hour outage at a western Canadian plant.

cards.label: Restart blowers and return sludge pumps
Restart the influent pumps one at a time
Inspect wet well levels and reset tripped equipment
Log the outage, the restart times, and any abnormal findings
Restart the screens and grit equipment
Confirm power is restored and review the alarm list
Check the clarifiers and the disinfection system

tasks.explanation: Power and alarms are assessed first, pumping is restored before downstream equipment, and disinfection is verified before the event is documented.

tasks.prompt: Order an operator morning round that walks the plant from the headworks to the effluent outfall.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine start of shift round in dry weather, plant in normal operation.

cards.label: Check aeration basin air, dissolved oxygen readings, and foam
Check primary clarifier drives, blankets, and scum removal
Check the disinfection system and the effluent flow reading
Record the round findings and flag defects in the maintenance log
Review overnight flows, alarms, and lab results at the control panel
Check secondary clarifier blankets and return sludge operation
Inspect the headworks screens and grit units and note screenings levels

tasks.explanation: The round follows the flow path so upstream problems are seen before their downstream effects, and recording closes the round.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a shift handover between the outgoing and incoming operators.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: day shift handing over to the evening operator at a small western plant.

cards.label: Outgoing operator lists equipment out of service and any alarms still active
Outgoing operator completes the shift log with flows, settings, and lab results
Outgoing operator leaves only after the incoming operator confirms the handover
Both operators walk the critical units together and note tank levels
Incoming operator signs the log accepting responsibility for the plant
Incoming operator asks questions and confirms chemical and sludge inventories

tasks.explanation: Written records come before the joint walk, questions are resolved face to face, and responsibility transfers only on a signed acceptance.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator response as plant flow rises sharply during spring runoff and heavy rain.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: combined flows rising, all treatment units in service, supervisor aware.

cards.label: Bring the standby primary clarifier into service and even the flow split
Log peak flow, actions taken, and effluent observations once flows recede
Notify the supervisor if flows approach the plant wet weather limit
Watch secondary clarifier blankets and effluent quality more frequently
Confirm all screens and grit units are running on high cycle
Increase primary and secondary sludge withdrawal to keep blankets low

tasks.explanation: Capacity and low blankets are prepared before the peak, monitoring runs through the event, escalation precedes any limit being reached, and logging closes the event.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for hand raking a manual bar screen during a shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: manually raked coarse screen in the headworks channel.

cards.label: Transfer the screenings into the lined screenings container
Put on gloves and eye protection and check the portable gas monitor reading
Slow or divert flow in the screen channel using the upstream gate
Rake screenings from the bottom of the bars upward into the collection tray
Restore normal flow through the channel and record the amount removed
Wash down the screen area and the rake

tasks.explanation: Protective equipment and gas checking come first, flow is controlled before raking, screenings are contained before washdown, and flow restoration is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a mechanical bar screen after maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: mechanically raked screen with wash water and a screenings compactor.

cards.label: Inspect the screen, rake, and channel and confirm all tools are removed
Remove lockout devices and restore power to the screen panel
Start the screenings compactor
Start the screen drive and observe one full rake cycle
Place the screen in automatic mode and verify level based starting
Open the wash water supply valve

tasks.explanation: The channel is clear before power returns, wash water and the compactor are ready before screenings are produced, and automatic control is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for handling a full container of screenings through to disposal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filled screenings container at the headworks.

cards.label: Drain free liquid from the container back to the screen channel
Close and secure the container lid
Wash and return the empty container to the headworks
Arrange pickup by the approved disposal hauler
Record the container weight or volume in the solids log
Move the sealed container to the designated storage area

tasks.explanation: Liquid drains back to the process before the container is sealed, records are made before pickup, and the washed container returns last.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator response as the level difference across a mechanical screen keeps rising.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: differential level across the screen well above normal, flow still passing.

cards.label: Log the peak differential and the actions taken
Rake the upstream face by hand if debris is matted on the bars
Switch the screen to continuous rake operation
Check the wash water pressure and clear any blocked spray nozzles
Notify the supervisor if the differential still does not fall
Confirm the high differential on the level readings and by a visual check

tasks.explanation: The reading is confirmed before action, continuous raking and wash water are tried before hand work, and escalation follows a failed correction.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing an outdoor secondary clarifier for freeze up.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: outdoor clarifier staying in service through the western Canadian winter.

cards.label: Inspect the scum baffle and skimmer for free movement before ice forms
Confirm the walkway and bridge heating or ice control measures are working
Log the winter readiness checks and any parts still on order
Check and service the drive gearbox oil for cold weather grade
Verify the torque alarm and drive protection devices by test
Check that the effluent launder covers or ice management fittings are in place

tasks.explanation: Cold weather servicing and ice control come before protection tests, and the readiness record closes the preparation.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a screen channel out of service for cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: twin screen channels, one stays in service.

cards.label: Remove the lockout, refill the channel, and return it to standby
Apply lockout to the channel screen drive
Shift all flow to the channel that stays in service
Remove settled debris and wash the channel down
Close the inlet and outlet gates on the channel being removed
Drain the isolated channel back to the wet well

tasks.explanation: Flow is fully on the duty channel before isolation, draining precedes lockout and cleaning, and the channel is refilled only after lockout is cleared.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running a screenings washer compactor cycle.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: washer compactor receiving screenings from the mechanical screen.

cards.label: Tie off the filled bag and record the number of bags produced
Confirm the discharge bag or container is in place and not full
Start the compactor and feed screenings from the screen conveyor
Stop the feed and let the compactor complete its pressing cycle
Open the wash water supply to the compactor
Check that wash water drains freely and organics return to the channel

tasks.explanation: Containment and wash water are ready before screenings arrive, the press finishes its cycle before shutdown, and bagging and records close the task.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a weekly inspection of a mechanical screen drive and rake.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screen in service, inspection from the deck and drive platform only.

cards.label: Observe one full rake cycle for smooth travel and tooth engagement
Check the rake teeth and bars for bent or missing teeth
Test the high level alarm by the panel test function
Record findings and raise a work order for any defect found
Check chain or cable tension and lubrication points
Check the drive motor and gearbox for noise, heat, and oil level

tasks.explanation: The inspection moves from drive to rake to protection devices, and any defect found becomes a recorded work order.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing the manual bypass screen during a forecast storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: mechanical screen in service, bypass channel normally isolated.

cards.label: Brief the oncoming shift on when the bypass is to be opened
Stage a rake, gloves, and an empty screenings container at the channel
Confirm the channel level gauge or staff gauge is readable
Exercise the bypass channel gates and confirm they move freely
Log the preparation checks in the shift log
Inspect the bypass screen bars and clear any stored debris

tasks.explanation: The screen and gates are proven before equipment is staged, the crew is briefed on the trigger, and the checks are logged before the storm arrives.

tasks.prompt: Order a daily headworks inspection round, following the flow path.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine round covering screens, channels, and screenings handling.

cards.label: Check wash water pressure at the gauge
Check channel levels and compare them with the normal marks
Hose down splashed areas around the screen deck
Check screenings container fill level and odour control covers
Record levels, container status, and any defects in the log
Observe a screen rake cycle and listen for unusual drive noise

tasks.explanation: Levels and operation are observed before housekeeping, and the round ends with a complete record.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for clearing ice and frozen screenings from an outdoor screen in winter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: outdoor headworks in a western Canadian cold snap, screen still in service.

cards.label: Apply hot wash water to the bars to remove remaining ice
Break loose frozen screenings with a bar, working from the deck only
Run the screen on continuous cycle to clear loosened material
Confirm the heat tracing on the wash water line is on and working
Log the clearing and note any damaged teeth or bent bars
Put on cold weather protective gear and check footing on the deck

tasks.explanation: Safety and heat tracing come first, manual loosening precedes the powered cycle, hot water finishes the clearing, and damage is recorded last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking one of two grit channels out of service for cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: twin grit channels, one stays in service.

cards.label: Shift all flow to the channel that stays in service
Remove the collected grit and wash the channel down
Drain the isolated channel back to the wet well
Close the inlet gate on the channel being removed
Apply lockout to the channel rake and drive equipment
Remove the lockout and refill the channel before returning it to standby

tasks.explanation: Flow is fully on the duty channel before isolation, draining precedes lockout and cleaning, and the channel is refilled only after lockout is cleared.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting an aerated grit tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: aerated grit tank with air blowers, a grit pump, and a grit classifier.

cards.label: Start the grit pump on its timed cycle
Check that the discharged grit looks clean and low in organics
Open the tank inlet gate and admit flow
Direct pumped grit to the classifier
Start the air blower at a low setting
Adjust the air until a gentle rolling motion carries organics forward while grit settles

tasks.explanation: Flow and air establish the rolling pattern before grit is pumped, and the quality of the washed grit is the final check.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running and then shutting down a grit classifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screw type grit classifier receiving pumped grit slurry.

cards.label: Start the classifier screw drive
Stop the screw after the last grit has cleared the trough
Adjust wash water so grit discharges damp and organics return with the overflow
Stop the grit pump when the grit sump is emptied
Start the grit pump feeding slurry to the classifier
Open the classifier wash water supply
Close the wash water supply

tasks.explanation: Wash water and the screw run before slurry arrives so grit never packs the trough, and shutdown reverses the order so the screw clears before it stops.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a routine inspection of a vortex grit separator.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: vortex grit tank in normal service, inspection from the deck only.

cards.label: Check the grit pump cycle by listening for its timed run
Flush the grit line with water after sampling
Open the sample port and inspect the pumped grit quality
Observe the paddle rotation and the surface swirl pattern
Record the findings and any defects in the maintenance log
Check the drive motor and gearbox for noise, heat, and oil level

tasks.explanation: The inspection follows the equipment from drive to grit discharge, the line is flushed after sampling, and recording is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for checking horizontal velocity in a grit channel.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: rectangular grit channel, target velocity near 0.3 m/s to settle grit and pass organics.

cards.label: Adjust the channel gate or flow split and note the change in the log
Measure the water depth and the channel width
Compare the result with the target velocity for grit settling
Record the current plant flow from the influent meter
Calculate the wetted cross sectional area
Calculate velocity as flow divided by cross sectional area

tasks.explanation: Velocity cannot be calculated until flow and area are known, comparison follows the calculation, and adjustment is the final step.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for cleaning out a grit sump and its pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: grit sump below the aerated grit tank, work from the surface with a vacuum hose.

cards.label: Inspect the pump suction and the sump walls for damage
Apply lockout to the grit pump starter
Vacuum out the accumulated grit and wash water residue
Remove the lockout, restore the valves, and test run the pump
Test the atmosphere at the sump opening with a gas monitor
Isolate the sump by closing the tank drain and pump suction valves

tasks.explanation: Isolation and lockout precede gas testing and cleaning, inspection happens while the sump is empty, and a test run proves the pump before it returns to service.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for handling a full grit container through to disposal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filled grit container beside the classifier discharge.

cards.label: Check the drained grit for odour and cover the container
Stop the classifier discharge and let the container drain
Wash the empty container and return it to the classifier
Record the container weight or volume in the solids log
Arrange pickup by the approved disposal hauler
Move the covered container to the designated storage pad

tasks.explanation: Draining and covering precede moving, records precede pickup, and the washed container returns last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for adjusting aerated grit air when the grit is coming out dirty with organics.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: classifier grit dark and odorous, tank in normal service.

cards.label: Log the new air setting and the grit quality result
Inspect a sample of the discharged grit and note its appearance
Increase the air in one small step to strengthen the rolling motion
Check the current air valve position and blower output
Allow the tank pattern to stabilize for several minutes
Sample the discharged grit again and compare its appearance

tasks.explanation: The problem is confirmed by sampling before air is changed, one small step is proven by a second sample, and the new setting is logged last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a primary clarifier taken out of service last week.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty primary clarifier with a sludge collection drive.

cards.label: Start the collector drive as the tank fills
Open the inlet gate and fill the clarifier
Inspect the drive, scrapers, and scum skimmer and clear all debris
Check effluent clarity and scum skimming once flow is steady
Close the drain valve and open the sludge withdrawal line
Set the sludge pump on a timed withdrawal cycle

tasks.explanation: The tank is inspected empty, filling precedes the timed withdrawal setup, and clarity is checked at steady flow.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for withdrawing sludge from a primary clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: manual withdrawal through a telescoping valve to the thickener.

cards.label: Measure the sludge blanket depth with a core sampler
Line up the withdrawal valves from the clarifier to the thickener
Watch the sludge at the sample port for density and colour
Close the valve when the draw off turns thin and watery
Open the withdrawal valve slowly and start the draw off
Record the withdrawal time and the new blanket depth

tasks.explanation: Blanket depth decides whether to withdraw, density at the sample port decides when to stop, and the closing blanket check is recorded last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for clearing scum from a primary clarifier surface.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clarifier with a rotating scum skimmer and a scum pump.

cards.label: Flush the scum box with plant water to move solids into the trough
Log the scum removal and the pit level
Rotate the skimmer to push scum toward the scum box
Check that the scum baffle is in place and undamaged
Flush the scum line clear with water
Start the scum pump and empty the scum pit

tasks.explanation: Scum must reach the box before flushing helps, the pit is pumped before the line is flushed, and logging finishes the task.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a primary clarifier out of service for the season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one of three primary clarifiers, the other two remain in service.

cards.label: Withdraw the accumulated sludge blanket to the thickener
Shift the flow split so the other clarifiers take the full flow
Stop the collector drive and apply lockout
Close the inlet gate to the clarifier being removed
Drain the supernatant back to the plant inlet
Wash down the tank and leave it empty and secured

tasks.explanation: Flow leaves first, sludge is removed before draining so it is not stranded, lockout follows the drive stop, and washdown is last.

tasks.prompt: Order an operator daily inspection round on a primary clarifier, following the walkway route.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine round, starting at the drive bridge and ending at the outlet end.

cards.label: Adjust the withdrawal cycle based on the blanket reading and record the round
Check influent distribution and flow split at the inlet well
Measure the sludge blanket depth near the outlet end
Check the drive unit for torque alarms, noise, and oil level at the bridge
Check effluent clarity and launder cleanliness at the outlet
Observe the scum skimmer and baffle condition along the surface

tasks.explanation: The round follows the physical route from drive to outlet, the blanket reading drives the withdrawal adjustment, and recording closes the round.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a primary clarifier sludge blanket found near the surface.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: blanket measured within 0.5 m of the surface, effluent solids rising.

cards.label: Notify the supervisor and log the event if the blanket still does not fall
Recheck the blanket depth after one withdrawal cycle
Reduce the flow split to this clarifier if the blanket stays high
Confirm the blanket depth with a second core sample
Increase the withdrawal rate or cycle duration
Check that the sludge pump and withdrawal line are operating

tasks.explanation: The reading is confirmed before equipment checks, withdrawal is increased before flow is cut, and escalation follows a failed recheck.

tasks.prompt: Order the response for a primary clarifier during a heavy rain flow surge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant flow at twice the dry weather average and still rising.

cards.label: Increase sludge withdrawal to keep blankets low ahead of the peak
Restore the normal flow split and withdrawal cycle after the peak passes
Monitor effluent suspended solids at the clarifier outlet
Confirm the flow split is even across all clarifiers in service
Check scum baffles and skimmers more frequently during the surge

tasks.explanation: Even splitting and low blankets prepare the tanks before the peak arrives, monitoring runs through the surge, and normal settings return only after it passes.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a chemical feed to a primary clarifier for enhanced settling.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alum feed system, dose already set by the supervisor from jar testing.

cards.label: Monitor clarifier effluent quality and record the dose and tank level
Confirm the approved dose and the injection point with the supervisor
Set the pump stroke to deliver the approved dose
Check the chemical storage tank level and the feed line condition
Verify chemical is reaching the injection point
Start the chemical feed pump

tasks.explanation: Authority and supply come before the pump starts, delivery is verified at the injection point, and effluent response is monitored last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for returning a drained primary clarifier to service after inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: circular clarifier emptied for inspection, drive and scraper repaired.

cards.label: Open the inlet gate and begin filling the clarifier slowly
Check effluent clarity at the launder before full loading
Start the scraper drive once the tank is filling
Start sludge withdrawal on a timed cycle once a blanket begins to form
Inspect the tank, drive, and scraper and remove all tools and debris
Close the drain valve and confirm the sludge outlet line is open

tasks.explanation: Tools are out before filling, the drive starts as water enters, sludge withdrawal waits until a blanket exists, and clarity is confirmed last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for changing over from a running primary sludge pump to the standby pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex primary sludge pumps with a common discharge to the thickener.

cards.label: Stop the duty pump once the standby pump is carrying the flow
Confirm the standby pump is primed and its valves are lined up
Start the standby pump and watch its discharge pressure build
Close the duty pump discharge valve and open its drain to check for leaks
Set the standby pump timer for the normal withdrawal cycle
Log the changeover and the reason for it

tasks.explanation: The standby pump proves itself under load before the duty pump stops, isolation follows, and the timer and log complete the changeover.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for balancing flow between two primary clarifiers.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two clarifiers in service, one showing a much deeper blanket than the other.

cards.label: Check the inlet gate positions against the flow split record
Measure the blanket depth and check effluent clarity in both clarifiers
Record the new gate positions and blanket readings
Open the gate on the lightly loaded clarifier to take the shifted flow
Adjust the inlet gate on the overloaded clarifier down in one small step
Recheck blankets and clarity after the tanks settle at the new split

tasks.explanation: Both tanks are measured before gates move, the overloaded tank is relieved before the other takes more, and the new split is proven by a recheck.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for washing down primary clarifier launders with algae growth.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: launders and weirs with visible algae, clarifier stays in service.

cards.label: Hose the loosened algae into the launder flow with plant water
Put on gloves and confirm safe footing on the walkway
Brush the launder walls and weir plates working from inlet toward outlet
Confirm effluent clarity at the outlet after the washdown
Record the washdown in the routine maintenance log
Check that the scum baffle has not been displaced by the brushing

tasks.explanation: Brushing follows the flow direction so loosened material leaves with the effluent, the baffle and clarity are checked after, and the work is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for seeding a new aeration tank to start activated sludge treatment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: new aeration tank filled with primary effluent, seed sludge available by tanker.

cards.label: Begin feeding primary effluent at a low rate
Discharge the seed sludge tanker into the aeration tank
Increase feed gradually as settleability and clarity improve
Mix and aerate the seeded contents for several hours without feed
Hold wasting to a minimum while the solids inventory builds
Measure dissolved oxygen, pH, and mixed liquor suspended solids
Fill the tank with primary effluent and start aeration

tasks.explanation: Seeding follows filling and aeration, a mixing period precedes feeding, measurements guide the ramp up, and wasting is held while inventory builds.

tasks.prompt: Order an operator morning process check routine for an activated sludge plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: start of day shift, plant in normal operation.

cards.label: Collect a mixed liquor sample for settleability and solids testing
Check blower operation and air header pressure at the blower room
Adjust air or return sludge settings based on the results
Observe mixed liquor colour and foam on the basin surface
Enter the observations and changes in the process log
Review overnight dissolved oxygen and flow trends on the control system
Measure dissolved oxygen in the aeration basin with a handheld meter

tasks.explanation: Trends are reviewed before field checks, samples are taken before settings change, and adjustments are made only from the gathered results.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for increasing the return activated sludge rate.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: secondary clarifier blanket rising, supervisor has approved a higher return rate.

cards.label: Wait and observe the clarifier blanket response
Remeasure the blanket depth before making any further change
Log the new return rate and the blanket readings
Adjust the return pump speed or valve in one small step
Confirm the new target return rate as a percent of influent flow
Review the clarifier blanket depth and the mixed liquor solids results

tasks.explanation: Data and the approved target come before the adjustment, and one small step is proven by a blanket remeasurement before any further change.
